newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs seen lower, pork bellies sharply lower.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs seen lower, pork bellies sharply lower.

text.p: CME hog futures were expected to open 0.200 to 0.250 cent per lb lower while pork belly futures were called 1.500 to 2.500 cent lower, livestock analysts said.

Carryover pressure in both pits was expected to stem from the cut by USDA in its pork export projections. This sparked an active selloff Thursday that took hog futures down sharply and pork bellies down the three-cent limit to two-month lows, analysts said.
USDA lowered 1997 projected pork exports by 105 million lbs to 1.250 billion lbs and lowered 1998 projections by 115 million lbs to 1.465 billion lbs.

Lower cash hog indications and falling wholesale pork prices this week should also weigh on hog futures. However, losses may be limited by an oversold condition and expectations of lighter hog marketings during the summer, analysts said.

The rising rate of hog slaughter compared to last year and lighter-than-expected domestic and export demand should also weigh on pork belly futures. Hog slaughter rates are now running above the year-ago level which adds to product offerings, traders said. Cash bellies have declined to lows levels since May, they added.
